title: Pardons Angela Stanton
description_medium: On February 18, 2020, President Donald Trump pardoned Angela Ronae Stanton, whose federal conviction involved conspiring to transport a stolen vehicle across state lines and tampering with its vehicle identification number. The Justice Department's clemency record lists time served and three years of supervised release, including six months of home confinement. It gives no reason for the pardon.
description_long: President Donald Trump granted Angela Ronae Stanton a pardon on February 18, 2020. The Justice Department record identifies her case in the Northern District of Georgia and lists a 2007 conviction for conspiracy to transport a stolen motor vehicle across state lines and tampering with a vehicle identification number. The sentence recorded was time served and three years of supervised release, with six months of home confinement. The entry documents the offense and sentence but does not describe Stanton's role, the circumstances of the case, advocacy for clemency, or the administration's reason for granting the pardon. A presidential pardon is distinct from a commutation: it forgives a federal offense and may restore certain rights, but it does not erase the historical conviction or establish innocence. The official clemency record is sufficient to describe who received relief and the federal case it covered, but it does not support a claim of political favoritism or an improper exchange.
